Problem: At a school, all 60 students play on at least one of three teams: Basketball, Soccer, and Mathletics. 8 students play all three sports, half the students play basketball, and the ratio of the size of the math team to the size of the basketball team to the size of the soccer team is $4:3:2$. How many students at the school play on exactly two teams?

Solve step by step. End with: The answer is [your answer].

message.content:
Since half of the 60 students play basketball,

\[
|B|=30
\]

The ratio of Mathletics : Basketball : Soccer is \(4:3:2\). Since basketball corresponds to \(3\) parts,

\[
3\text{ parts}=30 \implies 1\text{ part}=10
\]

So:

\[
|M|=40,\quad |B|=30,\quad |S|=20
\]

The sum of the team sizes is:

\[
40+30+20=90
\]

All 60 students play at least one sport, and 8 students play all three. Let \(x\) be the number of students who play exactly two teams.

Using inclusion-exclusion between the sum of team sizes and the total number of students:

\[
90 - (\text{pairwise overlaps}) + 8 = 60
\]

The pairwise overlaps count each exactly-two student once and each exactly-three student three times:

\[
\text{pairwise overlaps}=x+3(8)=x+24
\]

Thus:

\[
90-(x+24)+8=60
\]

\[
74-x=60
\]

\[
x=14
\]

The answer is 14.
